d1478b463999e146e17f61b5af99e9aca1549390.summary: SentinelLABS report on the Hafnium (aka Silk Typhoon) threat cluster and Chinese contractor firms linked to 2025 US indictments. It ties Shanghai Firetech and Shanghai Powerock to the Shanghai State Security Bureau, lists patented forensic and data-collection tools (including Apple file recovery), and revisits the 2021 Microsoft Exchange ProxyLogon campaign. Many links are hedged as unclear or possible.

hedges: The report says the tooling raises questions about the firms' ongoing work for the MSS and that attribution is difficult.
It is unclear how the ProxyLogon exploit proliferated ahead of the patch, and the exact date Hafnium's campaign began is unclear.
The report says it is unclear whether Shanghai Firetech offers offensive services to MSS offices beyond Shanghai; no public tenders or contracts were found.
The report says it is possible that none of the tooling it uncovered was ever deployed in offensive operations.
The report says Yin Kecheng's capacity (employee, subcontractor or jointly tasked) is unclear, and what of Yin's work Zhou tried to sell is unknown.
The report says it is unclear whether Chongqing Firetech's absence from the indictment means it was not involved in Hafnium-cluster activity.
The report raises as a possibility, not a finding, that the SSSB itself collected OrangeTsai's vulnerability research.
The report says there is good reason to believe only some of Shanghai Firetech's activities have been uncovered, and that other campaigns may exist under other names.
